headline: Your body was designed to move—sitting is the new smoking
universal_truth: Movement isn't just exercise—it's how your body maintains itself
fun_facts: A 20-minute walk can boost creative thinking by up to 60%
Prolonged sitting increases mortality risk even for people who exercise regularly
Your brain gets 15% more blood flow when you're walking than when you're sitting
discussion_questions: How much of your day is spent sitting versus moving?
What type of movement brings you joy, not just obligation?
How could you build more movement into your routine without 'exercise'?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: For millions of years, humans moved constantly—walking, running, climbing, building. Now we sit for an average of 10 hours a day. Our bodies haven't adapted. They still expect to move. Today, we explore what happens when they don't—and do.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Here's something troubling: even regular exercise doesn't fully offset the damage of prolonged sitting. If you work out for an hour then sit for eight, you're still at risk. What is it about sitting that's so harmful?

options.text: It slows metabolism and reduces blood flow throughout the body
options.response: Exactly. Sitting puts your body into a low-energy state that accumulates damage over time.

options.text: It's hard on your back and posture
options.response: Posture suffers, but the risks go much deeper...

q1.title: The Sitting Disease
q1.script: Sitting for more than 8 hours a day with no physical activity has a mortality risk similar to obesity and smoking. Your body interprets stillness as hibernation mode—metabolism slows, inflammation increases, and blood sugar regulation suffers.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "The Sitting Disease"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Movement and Mind
q2.script: A Stanford study found that walking increases creative output by an average of 60%. Your brain gets 15% more blood flow when moving. Movement isn't just for your body—it's how your brain thinks best.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Micro-Movements Matter
q3.script: The good news: frequent short movements help more than you'd expect. Standing up every 30 minutes, taking brief walks, using stairs—these 'movement snacks' throughout the day can significantly offset sitting's harms.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Your body is not a vehicle for transporting your brain to meetings. It's a system that needs movement to function. Find ways to move that feel like living, not like punishment.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 17. Tomorrow, we'll explore what happens when you rest—because movement and rest are partners. Until then, stand up, stretch, take a short walk. Your body will thank you.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Movement Snacks - Stand and Stretch
growTrack.learning_objective: Incorporate regular movement breaks into your day
growTrack.activity: Set a timer to stand up and move for 2 minutes every 30 minutes today. Walk around, stretch, do a few squats—anything that gets blood flowing. Notice how it affects your energy and focus.
